title: compress_schc_for_peer allow_fragmentation ignored on version-mismatch Rule 255
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs compress_schc_for_peer

The function compresses with peer.compress(ipv6, out, single_frame_limit) and only afterwards checks length > single_frame_limit && !allow_fragmentation.

For version-incompatible peers, AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext::compress uses encode_rule255(packet, out, single_frame_limit), which already errors when encoded size exceeds that limit. allow_fragmentation=true never runs: oversized Rule 255 (the only encoding a mismatch peer can send) fails with BufferTooSmall instead of returning a fragmentable SCHC packet.

Version-compatible peers are fine because compress() ignores single_frame_limit.

When allow_fragmentation is true, pass the fragmentation profile limit (SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE, or min(out.len(), SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE)) into peer.compress, and keep the single-frame ceiling only for the allow_fragmentation=false path.
acceptance_criteria: For a version-incompatible current peer, compress_schc_for_peer(..., single_frame_limit=MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET, allow_fragmentation=true) returns a Rule 255 packet larger than the single-frame ceiling when the IPv6 datagram requires it and fits the profile/out buffer. The same call with allow_fragmentation=false still returns InvalidPacket requiring authenticated fragmentation. Compatible-peer path unchanged.
